title: vbumper global configuration
description: Schema for the optional, per-user `~/.vbumpconfig.yaml` file: reusable named flows a project's own `.vbump.yaml` can pull in by name via `recall:` instead of redefining the same flow in every project. This file is never required to exist -- a project that never uses `recall:` is unaffected by its absence or content.

version.description: Schema version marker. Must be 3 for this format.

flows.description: Named flow definitions, each recallable from any project's own `.vbump.yaml` via `flows.<key>.recall`. A flow here is always a full definition -- it cannot itself set `recall`, so a global flow can never refer to another one.

flowKey.description: Identifier for a flow: lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, starting with a letter.

name.description: Human-readable display name for this flow (used in help/list output).

require_on_branch.description: Git branch that must be checked out for this flow to run (e.g. "develop", or a {NAME} placeholder such as "{DEVELOP_BRANCH}" resolved against this flow's own variables). Omit to allow the flow to run from any branch.

variables.description: Arbitrary flow-specific data, each entry available to this flow's commands as a {NAME} placeholder. A project recalling this flow may merge its own `variables` on top, key-by-key. Keys may not be VERSION or VERSION_TAG, which are always reserved for vbumper's own substitutions.

pre_commands.description: Commands run, in order, before version files are written back. If any command fails, the flow aborts immediately and no write-back or post_commands run.

post_commands.description: Commands run, in order, after version files are written back. If any command fails, the flow aborts immediately and no further post_commands run.

command.description: A single command, run through the operating system's own command shell after placeholder substitution (/bin/sh on Unix-like systems, cmd.exe on Windows). May contain the placeholders {VERSION}, {VERSION_TAG}, and one {NAME} placeholder per entry in this flow's own `variables:`. Substitution is verbatim -- no value is quoted or escaped on the command's behalf.
